title: Sync the knowledge bundle with what OpenCode support changed
action: Feature close for opencode-support: merge the behavior deltas of the twelve capped behavior_change cells into the touched area concepts, once, from evidence (capped cell traces, discovery.md, the judge verdicts on each cell's trace.semantic_judge) — never from plan.md and never from memory. Ask the CLI for the write target and frontmatter rather than picking paths by eye (bee knowledge check / bee knowledge context --work opencode-support; bee knowledge promote where a concept is new). What settled and must be readable without the code: bee now has THREE first-class runtimes, and OpenCode's hook belt is a checked-in TypeScript plugin rather than a rendered JSON manifest — a named per-runtime difference under the area's R1 rule, not drift; blocking on that belt is a thrown error because the runtime's before-tool surface has no abort field; the belt must honor verdicts that arrive at exit 0 (an argument repair, an ask) or the guard's dominant mechanism is inert; a coverage gate over a runtime's own tool registry is what keeps a newly registered write- or read-capable tool from silently bypassing the guard, and it has already caught two (apply_patch, lsp); an environment-gated proof must fail rather than skip, or it certifies nothing; and worker dispatch under that runtime is functional but sequential. Add Open Gaps for what is known-unserved (the model-guard dispatch branch that still resolves against a claude literal; nested-dispatch reservation identity; the CLI's subagent-selection fallback) rather than implying coverage. Keep business vocabulary outside Pointers: an area spec describes behavior, and a stranger with only the spec must be able to rebuild it. If a concept file's Pointers section still names a deleted Node-era file, correct it while you are there.

truths: Every claim traces to a capped cell, discovery.md, or a logged decision — no claim from plan.md or memory
The three-runtime reality and the plugin-as-third-belt difference are readable without the code

No spec text outside Pointers names a language, file, or framework
